record.original_question: In stochastic realizable contextual bandits, suppose (xt, ℓt) are drawn i.i.d. from a fixed distribution D, each policy class Πm is induced by a regression class Fm ⊂ (X × A → [0, 1]) via πf(x) = argmin_a f(x, a), and there exist m⋆ and f⋆ ∈ Fm⋆ such that E[ℓ(a) | x] = f⋆(x, a) for all contexts x and actions a. Is there, for some α ∈ [1/2, 1), an algorithm whose expected regret to the optimal policy πf⋆ is O(poly(K, M, log log |F|) · T^α log^(1−α) |Fm⋆|)? Alternatively, can one prove that no algorithm can achieve this guarantee for any α ∈ [1/2, 1)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 For some value α ∈ [1/2, 1), design an algorithm for contextual bandits that for any sequence F1 ⊂ F2 ⊂ ⋯FM = F, whenever data is stochastic and realizable, ensures E[ T ∑ t=1 ℓt(at) − T ∑ t=1 ℓt(πf⋆ (xt))] ≤ O(poly(K,M, log log∣F∣) ⋅ T α log1−α ∣Fm⋆ ∣). Alternatively, prove that no algorithm can achieve this guarantee for any value of α ∈ [1/2, 1).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the stochastic realizable contextual bandit problem with the following setup. Let X be a context space and A a finite action set with |A| = K. Pairs (x_t, ℓ_t) ∈ X × [0,1]^A are drawn i.i.d. from a fixed but unknown distribution D over T rounds. At each round t = 1, …, T, the learner observes x_t, selects an action a_t ∈ A (possibly using past observations and external randomness), and then observes only the loss ℓ_t(a_t) ∈ [0,1].

Fix M and a nested sequence of regression function classes F_1 ⊂ F_2 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_M = F, where each f ∈ F maps X × A → [0,1]. Each class F_m induces a policy class Π_m via π_f(x) = argmin_{a ∈ A} f(x, a). Assume the realizability condition: there exist an index m⋆ ∈ {1, …, M} and a function f⋆ ∈ F_{m⋆} such that

E_{(x,ℓ) ∼ D}[ℓ(a) | x] = f⋆(x, a) for all x ∈ X and a ∈ A.

The learner does not know m⋆. Define the regret with respect to the optimal policy π_{f⋆} as

R(T) = E[ Σ_{t=1}^T ℓ_t(a_t) − Σ_{t=1}^T ℓ_t(π_{f⋆}(x_t)) ].

Question. Does there exist a value α ∈ [1/2, 1) and an algorithm such that, for every nested sequence F_1 ⊂ ⋯ ⊂ F_M = F and every distribution D satisfying the realizability assumption above,

R(T) ≤ O( poly(K, M, log log |F|) · T^α · (log |F_{m⋆}|)^{1−α} ) ?

Alternatively, prove that no algorithm can attain such a guarantee for any α ∈ [1/2, 1).
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as a COLT 2020 open problem. Subsequent work, notably "Optimal Model Selection in Contextual Bandits with Many Classes via Offline Oracles" (Krishnamurthy & Athey, 2021), provides model-selection guarantees under stochastic realizability that approach the desired form, but only under additional conditions (sufficiently large horizon or assumptions enabling misspecification detection). A fully unconditional resolution—either a positive algorithm matching the stated bound for all instances or a matching impossibility result for every α ∈ [1/2, 1)—does not appear to be established in the literature, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Open Problem: Model Selection for Contextual Bandits
status_evidence.snippet: Open Problem 2 ... For some value α ∈ [1/2, 1), design an algorithm ... ensures regret ≤ O(poly(K,M,log log|F|) · T^α log^{1−α}|F_{m⋆}|).

status_evidence.title: Optimal Model Selection in Contextual Bandits with Many Classes via Offline Oracles
status_evidence.snippet: When one of the classes in the set is realizable, up to a logarithmic dependency on the number of classes, the algorithm attains optimal realizability-based regret bounds for that class under one of two conditions: if the time-horizon is large enough, or if an assumption that helps with detecting misspecification holds.
status_evidence.claim: Provides partial progress under additional conditions, not a full unconditional resolution.
